$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-SAF-005 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §7.6 and the RF-SAF-005 inventory entry. Architecture-source rule: evidence_claim_ids intentionally empty per v1.2 §4.3. Expresses uncertainty/safety STRUCTURE only for inability to safely assess: record cannot_assess and never coerce it to positive or negative. No diagnosis, rehab, dosage, progression, confidence, or return-to-sport logic. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.

input_contract.$comment: Structural trigger signals taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §7.6. Categorical only.

decision_contract.$comment: Uncertainty-preserving structure only. Records cannot_assess and does not convert it to positive or negative. No rehab authorization, no diagnosis, no numeric values.

notes: Architecture normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. No evidence_claim_ids are cited (legitimately empty per v1.2 §4.3 — architecture rules need not invent evidence claims). Per v1.2 §7.6 the trigger records cannot_assess and must NOT be converted to positive or negative; permitted responses are: use alternative evidence, widen the relevant confidence object, block the test, or refer when the unresolved uncertainty concerns a must-not-miss condition. Safety-state choice: §7.6 does not assign one fixed safety state; it lists conditional responses, one of which is 'block the test'. The most conservative structurally appropriate closed state for 'a self-test cannot safely proceed' is TEST_BLOCKED (V3.1 §21), so safety_state_output is TEST_BLOCKED with blocked_targets ['test']. The conditional escalation to a referral when the uncertainty concerns a must-not-miss condition is captured structurally in decision_contract (escalation_to_referral_when) without asserting it always fires — no clinical meaning invented. Draft — approval_status remains pending.
